sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Java testing interview questions cover the full testing pyramid — unit testing with JUnit 5 (lifecycle, parameterized tests, extensions), mocking with Mockito (verify, argument matchers, when not to mock), Spring Boot test slices, integration testing with Testcontainers, contract testing (Pact, Spring Cloud Contract), TDD discipline, performance testing, chaos testing, and the trade-offs between mocks vs real dependencies. This page covers JUnit, Mockito, Testcontainers and the testing-strategy questions that come up at every level.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Pyramid order: **unit > integration > E2E**.

- **Unit** — JUnit 5; isolate with Mockito.
- **Integration** — `@SpringBootTest` + Testcontainers (real DB, real Kafka).
- **E2E** — slow, flaky; reserve for the critical user journeys.
- **Contract** — Pact / Spring Cloud Contract; the seam between services.
- **Mutation** (PIT) — find what your tests *don't* cover.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Don't mock what you don't own** — tests become coupled to upstream APIs.
- **Testcontainers > H2** — same DB engine as prod or your test is lying.
- **`@SpyBean` is a smell** — usually means the seam is wrong.
- **Flakiness** — almost always async timing or shared state; fix the cause, don't `Thread.sleep`.
- **TDD vs test-after** — TDD when the design is unclear; test-after when it's a refactor.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd unit-test the pure logic, integration-test the wiring with Testcontainers, contract-test the public API, and reserve E2E for the smoke-critical paths. Coverage is a signal, not a goal — mutation testing tells me whether tests *assert* anything."*
